## Verdict

**Acme Desk** costs least for a team of 35, at **$280 per month**. Its $8 per-seat rate is the lowest on the list and its 10-seat minimum sits well below the team size, so all 35 seats are billed at list with no padding. Fennel HQ is next at $420; Kelp is $850, inflated by a 50-seat minimum that forces payment for 15 unused seats.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $8 | 10 |
| Fennel HQ | $12 | 25 |
| Kelp | $17 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 35 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Acme Desk:** minimum 10 < 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $8 = **$280 per month**. Effective rate $8.00 per person.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 25 < 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $12 = **$420 per month**. Effective rate $12.00 per person.
- **Kelp:** minimum 50 > 35, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $17 = **$850 per month**. Effective rate $24.29 per person ($850 ÷ 35).

Acme Desk is $140 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ and $570 per month cheaper than Kelp — $1,680 and $6,840 per year respectively.

## Risks

Kelp's penalty is a minimum-seat artefact: its $850 is fixed until headcount reaches 50, at which point its effective rate falls to $17. Even then it remains the dearest per seat, so it does not overtake Acme Desk at any size on list price alone.

Growth does not change the order. All three minimums are at or below 50 seats, and Acme Desk holds the lowest per-seat rate, so its lead widens in absolute terms as the team grows. Shrinking below 25 people would drop Fennel HQ to its $300 floor and below 10 would put Acme Desk on an $80 floor.

This is a price comparison only. The list carries no detail on features, support tiers, usage limits, security or integrations, so the cheapest seat may not be the comparable product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, negotiated discounts, onboarding and migration costs are not in the source and could reorder these totals.
